title: Past perfect and past perfect continuous
titleVi: Quá khứ hoàn thành và quá khứ hoàn thành tiếp diễn
summary: Đặt hai sự kiện quá khứ theo đúng thứ tự thời gian — chìa khoá để kể chuyện và viết bối cảnh lịch sử mạch lạc.
whyItMatters: Task 1 mô tả dữ liệu có nhiều mốc thời gian, và Task 2 thường cần bối cảnh lịch sử (*By 1990, the city had already lost most of its wetlands*). Thiếu `past perfect` khiến người đọc không biết việc nào xảy ra trước; dùng thừa lại làm câu văn nặng nề. Kiểm soát được ranh giới này là dấu hiệu của band 7.5+.

sections.heading: Past perfect: the earlier of two past events
body: The past perfect is **had + past participle**. It marks an action that happened before another past moment — the 'past of the past'.
The later event stays in the past simple: *When I arrived, the film had already started.* The starting happened first; my arrival came second.
Without a second past reference, the past perfect usually has no job to do. *I had seen him yesterday* sounds odd because there is nothing for it to be earlier than.

examples.right: When I arrived, the film had already started.
She had never flown before that trip.
examples.note: Experience up to a past point.

examples.right: The council had approved the plan before the consultation closed.
When I got to the station, the train had left.
examples.wrong: When I got to the station, the train already left.
examples.note: Vietnamese has no separate form here, but English needs **had left**.

sections.heading: When the past perfect is optional — and when it is not
body: With **before**, **after** and **already**, the order is often clear from the conjunction alone, so the past simple is acceptable: *After he ate, he went out.* The past perfect (*After he had eaten, he went out*) is more formal and more explicit.

But when the sequence is not obvious, or when you need to show that an event was completed before a second one, the past perfect is obligatory: *The building had been evacuated before the fire spread.* Without **had been**, the sentence suggests the evacuation happened at the same time as the fire.
In narrative writing, use the past perfect sparingly — one clause to set up the background, then return to the past simple for the events.

examples.right: After he had eaten, he went out.
examples.note: Formal and explicit; the past simple also works here.

examples.right: The building had been evacuated before the fire spread.
examples.wrong: The building was evacuated before the fire spread.
examples.note: **had been evacuated** makes the earlier completion unambiguous.

examples.right: I didn't know that she had resigned.
examples.note: Reporting an earlier event from a past viewpoint.

sections.heading: Past perfect continuous: duration before a past point
body: The past perfect continuous is **had been + -ing**. It describes an activity that had been going on for some time before a past moment, often explaining a visible state at that moment.

Compare: *She had worked there for two years* (a completed period) and *She had been working there for two years when the factory closed* (duration leading up to the closure, with emphasis on the process).
It is the natural tense for cause and effect in the past: *The ground was saturated because it had been raining for days.*

examples.right: She was exhausted because she had been working since dawn.
They had been negotiating for months when the deal collapsed.
examples.note: Long process interrupted by a short event.

examples.right: The road was flooded; it had been raining for three days.
examples.wrong: The road was flooded; it had rained for three days.
examples.note: The continuous emphasises the unbroken process leading to the flood.

sections.heading: Past perfect with reporting and reasons
body: Reported speech and verbs of thinking often need the past perfect because the original statement was made in the past: *He said he had finished the report* (= he finished it before he spoke).
The same logic applies to explanations: *I was surprised that so few people had applied.* The applying happened before my surprise.
Keep the anchor clear. The anchor is the later past moment — the arrival, the statement, the surprise. Everything earlier takes **had**.

rows: She had left before I arrived.
She had been waiting for an hour.
the later event / the narrative line
He ate, then he went out.

sections.heading: Past perfect in IELTS Task 1 and Task 2
body: In Task 1, the past perfect is useful when a chart refers to a baseline that was already established before the period shown: *By 2000, the population had already passed one million, and it continued to grow.*
In Task 2, it handles historical background efficiently: *By the time legislation was introduced, the damage had been done.* This compresses two stages into one sentence.
Avoid stacking several past perfects in a row. One is enough to establish the earlier layer; after that, the past simple carries the story.

examples.right: By 2000, the population had already passed one million.
examples.note: A baseline established before the chart period.

examples.right: By the time legislation was introduced, the damage had been done.
examples.note: Passive past perfect compressing two stages.

examples.right: The scheme had been running for a decade before it was evaluated.

commonMistakes.wrong: When I arrived at the cinema, the film already started.
commonMistakes.right: When I arrived at the cinema, the film had already started.
commonMistakes.why: Cần `past perfect` để chỉ hành động xảy ra trước một mốc quá khứ khác. Tiếng Việt dùng 'đã' cho cả hai nên người học thường bỏ mất `had`.

commonMistakes.wrong: She had been working there for two years before she had left.
commonMistakes.right: She had been working there for two years before she left.
commonMistakes.why: Chỉ mệnh đề chỉ hành động xảy ra trước mới dùng `past perfect`; mệnh đề sau `before` giữ `past simple`.

commonMistakes.wrong: I had seen him yesterday at the market.
commonMistakes.right: I saw him yesterday at the market.
commonMistakes.why: Không có mốc quá khứ thứ hai để so sánh thì `past perfect` là thừa. Một sự kiện quá khứ đơn lẻ dùng `past simple`.

commonMistakes.wrong: I was surprised that so few people applied.
commonMistakes.right: I was surprised that so few people had applied.
commonMistakes.why: Việc nộp đơn xảy ra trước cảm giác ngạc nhiên, nên cần `past perfect`. Thiếu `had` khiến hai việc có vẻ đồng thời.

commonMistakes.wrong: The ground was wet because it had been rained all night.
commonMistakes.right: The ground was wet because it had been raining all night.
commonMistakes.why: `rain` là nội động từ, không có dạng bị động. Cấu trúc đúng là `had been + V-ing`.

ieltsTips: Trong Task 1, chỉ dùng `past perfect` khi biểu đồ có một mốc 'trước giai đoạn được mô tả'; nếu không, `past simple` là đủ và an toàn hơn.
Trong Task 2, dùng `By the time ..., ... had ...` để nén hai giai đoạn lịch sử vào một câu, giúp tiết kiệm từ và tạo nhịp học thuật.
Khi kể chuyện ở Speaking Part 2, một câu `past perfect` ở đầu để dựng bối cảnh là đủ; sau đó quay về `past simple` để câu chuyện chạy.
Đừng dùng `past perfect` chỉ vì câu có chữ `before` hoặc `after` — nếu trật tự đã rõ, `past simple` tự nhiên hơn và ít rủi ro hơn.

exercises.question: When we got to the theatre, the play ___.
options: already started
had already started
has already started
was already starting
exercises.explanation: Vở kịch bắt đầu trước khi chúng tôi đến → **past perfect**.

exercises.question: Which sentence is correct?
options: I had seen him yesterday at the market.
I saw him yesterday at the market.
I have seen him yesterday at the market.
I was seeing him yesterday at the market.
exercises.explanation: Một sự kiện quá khứ đơn lẻ, không có mốc so sánh thứ hai → **past simple**.

exercises.question: She was tired because she ___ since 5 a.m.
options: worked
had been working
has been working
was working
exercises.explanation: Hoạt động kéo dài trước một trạng thái trong quá khứ → **past perfect continuous**.

exercises.question: Which sentence shows that the evacuation happened first?
options: The building was evacuated before the fire spread.
The building had been evacuated before the fire spread.
The building is evacuated before the fire spread.
The building has been evacuated before the fire spread.
exercises.explanation: **had been evacuated** xác lập rõ hành động hoàn tất trước khi đám cháy lan.

exercises.question: Which sentence combines the past perfect continuous and the past simple correctly?
options: She had been working there for two years before she had left.
She had been working there for two years before she left.
She was working there for two years before she had left.
She has been working there for two years before she left.
exercises.explanation: Chỉ mệnh đề trước dùng **past perfect**; mệnh đề sau **before** dùng **past simple**.

exercises.question: By the time the ambulance arrived, the patient ___ (regain) consciousness.
exercises.explanation: Hành động hoàn tất trước mốc **arrived** → past perfect.

exercises.question: The streets were empty because everyone ___ (go) home early.
exercises.hint: nguyên nhân của trạng thái quá khứ
exercises.explanation: Việc về nhà xảy ra trước trạng thái đường vắng → past perfect.

exercises.question: They ___ (negotiate) for six months when the deal finally collapsed.
exercises.explanation: Quá trình kéo dài trước sự kiện **collapsed** → past perfect continuous.

exercises.question: I was surprised that so few candidates ___ (apply) for the scholarship.
exercises.explanation: Việc nộp đơn xảy ra trước **was surprised** → past perfect.

exercises.question: By 1990, the city ___ (already / lose) most of its wetlands.
exercises.explanation: **By + mốc quá khứ** đánh dấu hành động hoàn tất trước mốc đó → past perfect.
